in_text_mentions: r minute. Her body temperature was 37.1°C. Heart and lung sounds were normal. Ophthalmologic examination revealed that visual acuity was 0.1 bilaterally, and intraocular pressure was 15 mmHg in both eyes. On biomicroscopy, bilateral ciliary hyperemia, cataract, and interstitial keratitis with marginal infiltrates were noticed (Figure 1). The fundus examination revealed mild hyperemia of both optic discs, with blurred borders, and no signs of vitreous or retinal inflammation. Pure tone audiogram (PTA) and auditory brainstem responses (ABR) showed bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (Figure 2).

plate_findings.evidence: PET-CT demonstrates increased 18F-FDG uptake (aortic wall enhancement) in the aortic arch, consistent with inflammatory aortitis

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Real patient PET-CT image showing increased 18F-FDG uptake in the subclavian and common carotid arteries, a recognized variant manifestation of systemic large-vessel vasculitis in Cogan syndrome, as described in the article caption. B: Real patient PET-CT image showing increased 18F-FDG uptake in the aortic arch, corresponding to inflammatory aortitis (aortic wall thickening/enhancement), a recognized variant manifestation of Cogan syndrome. C: Real patient PET-CT image showing increased 18F-FDG uptake in the thoracic aorta, corresponding to inflammatory aortitis (aortic wall thickening/enhancement), a recognized variant manifestation of Cogan syndrome. D: Real patient PET-CT image showing increased 18F-FDG uptake in the coronary arteries, a recognized variant manifestation of coronary vasculitis in Cogan syndrome, as described in the article caption.
panels.attribution_text: Na et al. A case report of Cogan's syndrome with recurrent coronary stenosis.. Frontiers in cardiovascular medicine 2024. doi:10.3389/fcvm.2024.1451113. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: PET-CT showed an increased circular and linear 18F-FDG uptake in the subclavian and common carotid arteries (A), aortic arch (B), thoracic aorta (C), and coronary (D).
in_text_mentions: Upon review, coronary angiography (CAG) showed in-stent restenosis (Figure 1). Echocardiography revealed thinning of the left ventricular inferior wall basal segment, mild aortic regurgitation, and decreased left ventricular diastolic function. Positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) demonstrated an increased uptake of (18)F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) in the aorta and its primary branches, as well as in the coronary arteries (Figure 3).

FA showed fluorescent leakage from both retinal arteries and veins, hemorrhagic blockage on the nasal side of the right eye (Figure 3C), and extensive arterial occlusion on the temporal retina of the left eye (Figure 3D). panels.rationale: Slit-lamp photograph of the right cornea in a Cogan syndrome case report, showing superior deep stromal opacity with vascularisation/ghost vessels, matching the vocabulary findings for interstitial keratitis and deep corneal neovascularization.
panels.attribution_text: Pherwani et al. Cystoid macular oedema in Cogans syndrome-a case report.. Cases journal 2008. doi:10.1186/1757-1626-1-339. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Right cornea showing stromal opacity with vascularisation in the superior aspect.
in_text_mentions: Two years later the patient presented with blurred and distorted vision in both eyes. Aided Snellen's acuity was 6/9 bilaterally. The right cornea still had the deep stromal opacity with ghost vessels superiorly (fig 1). There was mild anterior uveitis. There was mild anterior uveitis and bilateral cystoid macular edema (CMO) (fig 2 and 3). Topical steroids and ketorolac were commenced. Blood tests revealed a raised ESR, serology for autoantibodies, Treponema and Borrelia, serum ACE, chest X ray were normal.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Slit-lamp anterior segment photograph of the right eye in a case of atypical Cogan syndrome showing anterior chamber inflammatory cells and keratic precipitates; uveitis is a recognized ocular manifestation of Cogan syndrome although IK was absent. Eye is dilated; surrounding skin visible and light-toned. B: Slit-lamp photograph of the left eye in the same atypical Cogan syndrome case, with arrows marking posterior iris synechiae plus inflammatory cells and keratic precipitates; an ocular inflammatory manifestation in a confirmed Cogan syndrome patient. Eyelid skin visible, light-toned.
panels.attribution_text: Inokuchi et al. A Case of Bilateral Retinal Vasculitis in Atypical Cogan Syndrome.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.66984. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Anterior segment images at the initial examination (A) Right and (B) left. Inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber and keratic precipitate were observed in both eyes. Posterior iris synechiae were seen in the left eye (B: arrows). No IK was found in both eyes. IK: Interstitial keratitis
in_text_mentions: Ophthalmological examination revealed that her right CVA and left CVA were 1.0 and 0.09, respectively. Slit-lamp microscopy revealed inflammatory cells, posterior corneal deposits in both eyes, and posterior iris synechia in the left eye; however, IK was not observed (Figures 2A, 2B).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Low-power H&E of the patient's erythematous skin lesion showing inflammatory infiltrate around small vessels in dermis/subcutaneous tissue, a cutaneous manifestation in this atypical Cogan syndrome case; no matching vocabulary finding key exists, so findings are listed as proposed terms. B: High-magnification H&E of the same patient's skin showing fractured-nuclei leukocytes around a capillary (arrow), described as similar to leukocytoclastic vasculitis; a recognized cutaneous manifestation in this atypical Cogan syndrome report, though not covered by the supplied vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Inokuchi et al. A Case of Bilateral Retinal Vasculitis in Atypical Cogan Syndrome.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.66984. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Dermatopathological findings of multiple erythema (A) Inflammatory cell infiltration was observed mainly around small blood vessels in the dermis to subcutaneous adipose tissue enclosed by a white dotted line. (B) High magnification of (A). Leukocytes, in which the nuclei were fractured, were infiltrated around the small vessels. Similar histology was seen in leukocytoclastic vasculitis. The arrow indicates capillary.
in_text_mentions: ide (Figure 1B). Histological examination of the erythematous lesions showed inflammatory cell infiltration, mainly around small blood vessels in the dermis to the subcutaneous adipose tissue (Figure 4A). At high magnification, it was observed that leukocytes with fractured nuclei infiltrated the small vessels, which is also seen in the histology of leukocytoclastic vasculitis (Figure 4B). The inflammatory cells were predominantly neutrophils and histiocytes with a small number of T lymphocytes.
